forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Devon auditors to assess council's action on schools-funding deficit and its Safety Valve Programme work
news_drafts.lead:
Devon County Council's external auditor, the independent check on its accounts, will examine what the council has done to reduce its annual deficit on the dedicated schools grant (DSG), according to an audit progress report for the Audit Committee meeting of 30 September. The DSG is the government grant that funds schools, and a deficit on it is usually an overspend on support for children with special needs.

The review forms part of the auditor's value for money judgement, its separate view on whether the council manages its money and decisions properly, under the heading of financial sustainability. The report says the auditor will assess the actions taken "to reduce the annual DSG deficit in order to protect the cash position and increase financial resilience in the medium term". That includes how the council "has worked within the Safety Valve Programme".

The auditor will also look at how the council's medium-term financial strategy, its plan for the next three to five years, provides for council contributions towards reducing the deficit. The paper gives no figure for the deficit or for those contributions.

findings.paper_title: 16.06.2026 Alison McGovern MP response to Audit Committee LGR Risks
findings.headline: Government confirms new unitary councils will take full council roles from April 2028
findings.detail: The government remains on track with the published timetable, with new unitary councils taking full council roles from April 2028 (subject to parliamentary approval) following shadow council elections in May 2027. Existing councils must continue delivering services and fulfilling duties until vesting day while preparing for transfer.
findings.matters: The confirmed timeline means Devon faces approximately 19 months of transition period requiring parallel running costs and dual-system management while maintaining service delivery.
findings.figures: Shadow council elections May 2027; unitary councils operational from April 2028
findings.quote: Subject to parliamentary approval, we expect new unitary councils to take on full council roles from April 2028, with elections to new shadow councils in May 2027.

findings.paper_title: 16.06.2026 Alison McGovern MP response to Audit Committee LGR Risks
findings.headline: Government states that councils bear responsibility for managing budgets during local government reorganisation
findings.detail: In response to financial sustainability concerns, the government states: It is the responsibility of councils to manage their budgets and work through the implications relating to local government reorganisation. This indicates the government is not committing specific financial support for transition costs.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know whether reorganisation costs will be met by government or absorbed by the council; this response places the burden squarely on Devon.
findings.quote: It is the responsibility of councils to manage their budgets and work through the implications relating to local government reorganisation.

findings.paper_title: 16.06.2026 Alison McGovern MP response to Audit Committee LGR Risks
findings.headline: Devon's Audit Committee formally raised concerns about financial sustainability relating to local government reorganisation
findings.detail: The Audit Committee wrote to the Secretary of State on 26 May 2026 setting out views on governance, risk management and financial sustainability in relation to the proposed timeline for local government reorganisation in Devon, Plymouth and Torbay.
findings.matters: When an audit committee formally raises concerns about financial sustainability to government, it signals the council's leadership sees material risks to financial resilience during the transition.
findings.quote: setting out your views on governance, risk management and financial sustainability in relation to the proposed timeline for local government reorganisation in Devon, Plymouth and Torbay

findings.paper_title: DCC DPF Audit Progress report and sector update - DRAFT TO COUNCIL
findings.headline: Adults and Children's Services identified as financial sustainability risk area requiring scrutiny of cost management, demand reduction, and overspend mitigation.
findings.detail: Value for Money audit will examine actions taken to manage demand and costs, including demand reduction strategies, financial modelling, and mitigation of overspends. Children's Services additionally has improvement plan addressing prior Ofsted and CQC concerns, with auditors assessing progress and internal control strengthening.
findings.matters: These services typically represent over 50% of council spending. Combined focus on demand reduction, cost management, and overspend mitigation indicates material cost pressures and control environment concerns in the largest budget areas.
findings.quote: review the actions taken to manage demand and costs in relation to Adults and Children's Services. This includes actions taken to reduce demand, financial and demand modelling, mitigation of overspends and delivery of savings

findings.paper_title: DCC DPF Audit Progress report and sector update - DRAFT TO COUNCIL
findings.headline: Council depends on transformation programme to identify and deliver significant medium-term savings that remain unquantified.
findings.detail: Auditors will examine progress in 'identifying the significant savings required over the medium term' through the transformation programme. The use of 'identifying' rather than 'delivering' indicates material savings remain unscheduled, creating execution risk in medium-term financial planning.
findings.matters: Unidentified material savings indicate an unresolved budget gap. Execution risk on transformation delivery directly affects the council's capacity to deliver balanced budgets without further service reductions or alternative revenue sources.
findings.quote: determine the progress made developing the organisational wide approach to embedding the transformation programme and identifying the significant savings required over the medium term
